articles.title: US phases out financial aid for Namibia's HIV programs
articles.description: The United States plans to phase out financial support for Namibia's HIV response programs. The U.S. will provide $45 million for the 2027 fiscal year, after which Namibia will fund its own programs. The U.S. will only offer technical cooperation. Namibia has received around $45 million annually through the U.S. President’s Emergency Plan for AIDS Relief. The U.S. has contributed over $1.1 billion since 2003. While it has been on the cards through the phasing out of PEPFAR, the funding withdrawal follows Namibia’s rejection of data-sharing provisions, citing privacy and sovereignty concerns. The U.S. has signed agreements with about 30 countries, but some, like Ghana and Zimbabwe, have rejected similar terms.
